title: Trace a candidate through the release gates
description: Compare policies against the same prompt and generated candidate. Prompt risk, output risk, identity risk, review, and provenance stay separate so the final action is explainable.

policies.label: Prompt filter only
policies.detail: Blocks obvious requests before compute but publishes every admitted candidate without output review or provenance.

policies.label: Two-gate product policy
policies.detail: Inspects prompts and pixels, holds ambiguous identity-sensitive output, and attaches provenance to accepted assets.

policies.label: Strict publication policy
policies.detail: Uses lower thresholds and accountable review for a public channel with a small risk budget.

scenarios.label: Benign watercolor
scenarios.prompt: A watercolor of a quiet greenhouse at sunrise
scenarios.candidate: The output matches the requested scene and contains no identified person.
scenarios.lesson: A low-risk path should still produce a recorded, testable release decision.

scenarios.label: Public-figure poster
scenarios.prompt: A campaign-style poster featuring a well-known mayor
scenarios.candidate: The output resembles the named person and could be interpreted as endorsed campaign material.
scenarios.lesson: A prompt-only gate misses identity and context visible in the generated image.

scenarios.label: Ambiguous game artwork
scenarios.prompt: Cinematic battlefield concept art for a strategy game
scenarios.candidate: The sampled image contains graphic injury beyond the product's general-audience policy.
scenarios.lesson: Stochastic output can cross a policy boundary even when the request is not explicitly prohibited.

scenarios.label: Explicit prohibited request
scenarios.prompt: A clearly disallowed request under the configured product policy
scenarios.candidate: No candidate should be generated when admission policy can decide safely.
scenarios.lesson: Blocking before scheduling protects users and avoids unnecessary GPU work.
